root_cause.q1_which_path_allocates_without_row: None of the managent mint paths (suggest / add --auto) allocate an ID without writing a row — both mint the T-ID and write the row in ONE locked write (lockStore -> readState -> state.put -> sys_next_id += 1 -> writeStateLocked). The defect is not an allocation-without-row path; it is a ROW-LOSS path: the rows are written only to the uncommitted working-tree tasks.json, and a concurrent console re-serializes tasks.json from a stale in-memory snapshot before any commit captures the freshly-minted rows.
root_cause.q2_why_t674_t695_block_failed_while_t696: The block T663-T695 (not just the nine named: 33 IDs, next_id advanced 661 -> 696) was registered, dispatched, claimed and graded entirely inside the uncommitted working-tree store during 2026-08-22 20:19-23:29Z. The last committed store state on main was cca08cb (next_id=661); the rows that followed lived only in the working tree. T694's own findings record the symptom ('the live kanban store was cleared of the T690-T694 batch-2 rows mid-run by fleet housekeeping ... the rows were never in any committed store state'). T696+ registered normally because by then the sprint manager's commits and the working tree had re-converged on one store snapshot. The flock serializes concurrent managent writes, but it does NOT protect against (a) a git checkout/stash/reset reverting the working tree, (b) a managent process running against a different worktree, or (c) a long-lived process writing back a store it read much earlier — any of which clobbers uncommitted rows with no tombstone and no error.
root_cause.q3_lockfile_or_seat_habit: tasks.json.lockfile is NOT the defect — it correctly serializes managent writes; the loss happens at the git boundary (uncommitted working tree), which the flock cannot span. The implicated seat-side habit is the sprint-manager seat (T612/T278) doing housekeeping commits that re-serialize tasks.json from a stale snapshot, while lane rows were mid-flight. The verifiable evidence: git log -S '"T690"' -- docs/infra/managent/tasks.json is empty across ALL commits (same for all nine) — the rows never reached a committed store, so no archive tombstone exists. D038/D039 (2026-08-23) independently confirm the debris ('race-grading lanes purged by T612 housekeeping'; 'tasks T691/T692 are NOT registered; likely T706 batch2 debris').

mechanism.what: A bidirectional T-ID <-> findings census: the new `managent lanes` verb.
mechanism.forward: every findings/<T<id>>-*.json whose <id> has no row in tasks.json or archive.json is an UNREGISTERED lane (the T716 class). This is a GATE: `managent lanes` exits 1 when any exist, so the drift fails a run instead of surviving silently.
mechanism.reverse: every live done/failed row whose bundle declares a deliverables=findings/... path that never landed on disk is a MISSING-FINDINGS row. Flag-only, never deleted.
mechanism.backfill: `managent lanes --backfill [T<id> ...]` mints+closes the orphans (or the named subset) in ONE locked write: status done, verdict pass-with-findings, a note naming this findings file. An ID can never again outlive its row once the census is run.
mechanism.surfaced_in_orient: the worker preamble (`managent orient`) now prints one `lanes:` line with the two counts, so the drift is visible at dispatch-read time.
mechanism.tested: tools/regression-managent-lanes.sh (five arms, scratch repo only) is wired into `zig build test` in build.zig. The test is an invariant assertion (the defect was already reproduced on the live store before the fix; the pre-fix state IS the known-bad): arm A shows the gate RED on an orphaned finding, arm B shows --backfill mints+clears it, arm C shows a missing-findings row is flag-only and never deleted, arm D is the null control, arm E asserts the REAL live store is byte-identical throughout.

backfill.note: each minted row carries the note 'T716 backfill: minted+closed an orphaned lane' and an impression_waiver naming this findings file.

notes: Root cause: rows minted by suggest/add live only in the uncommitted working-tree tasks.json; concurrent console re-serialization (the sprint-manager seat's housekeeping commits, git stash/checkout, or a long-lived process writing a stale snapshot) clobbers them before any commit captures them. The ID stays allocated (next_id advanced, bundle written, findings graded) but the row vanishes with no tombstone and no error — and nothing detected it until this row. Fix: `managent lanes` (bidirectional census + --backfill), surfaced in `managent orient`, wired into `zig build test` via tools/regression-managent-lanes.sh. Backfilled the nine scoped rows (status done, verdict pass-with-findings). Reverse sweep flagged 5 done/failed rows whose declared findings never landed (flag-only, nothing deleted). Inbox polled empty at claim and before done; no T716-targeted directives to record. Pre-existing build flake observed once: `zig build` failed transiently on src/gtp.zig (version.banner) while tools/gen-version.sh regenerated version.zig; a re-run succeeded — unrelated to this change.
